Composition rule: Diagonal composition or Z-flow; place highest narrative weight on largest panel or on bottom-right
Character placement: Varied: 1-2 characters per panel max; position protagonist on golden points
Background continuity: Keep environment elements (skyline / horizon / furniture) consistent across all 4 panels
Prompt assembly rule: [establishing panel: environment + time] + [character panel: anchor verbatim + pose + expression] + [turn panel: action or dialogue beat] + [punchline panel: reaction or emotional close-up]
Visual rhythm control: Vary panel sizes: largest = climax of page; smallest = setup or transition. Use gutters 3-5mm
Common failure: P1 panels too uniform in size (no visual hierarchy); reading order ambiguous due to similar panel shapes

Panel arrangement: 3x2 (3 top / 3 bottom) or 2x3 (2 left / 2 middle / 2 right)
Composition rule: Horizontal emphasis for dialogue pages; vertical emphasis for action pages
Character placement: Dialogue pages: place speakers on alternating sides per 180-degree rule; action pages: motion direction across gutter
Background continuity: Environment establishes once in P1-2; P3-4 inherit same spatial layout; P5-6 may shift to close-up (blur background)
Prompt assembly rule: [P1-2: wide establishing + character intro] + [P3-4: dialogue A->B and B->A; preserve eyeline and axis] + [P5: action beat or twist] + [P6: reaction or resolution]
Visual rhythm control: Reserve one "hero panel" (largest or most detailed) per page for narrative focus. Use thinner gutters for faster rhythm
Common failure: Too many small panels (cluttered; reader loses focus); no clear hero panel; gutters inconsistent

Panel arrangement: Horizontal rectangular panels stacked vertically; width varies per beat pacing
Aspect ratio: Landscape (16:9 per panel) or portrait (full page width)
Composition rule: Wide = slow / contemplative; narrow = fast / tense / action
Character placement: Position characters on same horizontal plane across strip for continuity; use depth layers (foreground / midground / background)
Background continuity: Single continuous environment; background must connect seamlessly across panel boundaries
Prompt assembly rule: [beat 1: establishing wide] + [beat 2: medium dialogue or action] + [beat 3: close-up reaction or emotional peak] + [beat 4: resolution or transition to next strip]
Visual rhythm control: Panel width ratio: 40% / 25% / 20% / 15% for 4-panel strip (decelerating rhythm). Or 20% / 30% / 30% / 20% for symmetric tension
Common failure: Background jumps between panels (continuity break); character position drifts horizontally without motivation

Panel arrangement: Single panel fills entire page (or double-page spread)
Composition rule: Center composition or diagonal tension; use negative space deliberately
Character placement: All main characters visible; protagonist at visual center or on strong diagonal; supporting characters frame the edges
Background continuity: Maximum environmental detail; treat as a poster within the story
Prompt assembly rule: [all P0 anchors verbatim] + [peak action pose or emotional moment] + [dramatic lighting: single-source or rim light] + [environment reacting to the moment: wind / debris / light rays / crowd reaction]
Visual rhythm control: Use only for genuine climactic or emotionally pivotal moments. Maximum once every 8-10 pages
Common failure: Using splash page for non-climactic scene; too frequent usage kills pacing impact; cluttered composition (no breathing room)

Panel arrangement: Vertical stack of full-width panels; infinite scroll
Composition rule: One focal point per panel; reading direction purely top-to-bottom
Character placement: Character stays on same vertical axis (usually center or left third) for stability; action may break axis for impact
Background continuity: Environment recedes into distance; use atmospheric perspective (blur + desaturation) for background depth
Prompt assembly rule: [hook panel: close-up or extreme close-up with strong emotion] + [setup panels: environment + character intro] + [development panels: dialogue or action beats] + [climax panel: splash-like full-width] + [resolution panel: calm or cliffhanger]
Visual rhythm control: Panel height ratio: short (1:1) for beats / tall (2:3 or full width) for establishing or climax. Use parallax scrolling between panels if platform supports
Common failure: Panels too similar in height (monotonous rhythm); focal point jumps randomly (reader loses tracking); excessive text per panel on mobile
